descriptionAdvanced.en: The Misicuni Multipurpose Project is one of the most ambitious and long-awaited engineering feats in Bolivia's history. Located high in the Tunari mountain range, it centers around a 120-meter tall face-rockfill dam that captures water from the Misicuni and Viscas rivers. The project serves three vital functions: generating over 120 megawatts of clean hydroelectric energy, providing reliable drinking water to the growing city of Cochabamba, and irrigating thousands of hectares of fertile land in the central valley. Historically, the project faced decades of delays and challenges due to its extreme scale and the complexity of the Andean geology. Today, it stands as a symbol of regional progress and environmental management, significantly improving the quality of life for millions of people in the heart of the country.

en: The Misicuni dam is the highest in Bolivia, reaching a height of 120 meters.
The project includes a 20-kilometer-long tunnel that transports water through the mountains to the valley below.
The reservoir created by the dam has a storage capacity of over 180 million cubic meters of water.
The hydroelectric plant is a critical part of Bolivia's transition towards renewable energy sources.
